newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: ATHLETICS-TERGAT LOOKING TO EMULATE NGUGI'S ACHIEVEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TERGAT LOOKING TO EMULATE NGUGI'S ACHIEVEMENTS.

text.p: Kenyan Paul Tergat, the Olympic 10,000 metres silver medallist, said on Monday he wants to emulate compatriot John Ngugi and win six world cross country titles.

But Tergat, favourite to win Wednesday's inaugural Race Through History around the 2,000-year-old Kalemegdan Fortress which overlooks the confluence of the Danube and Sava rivers, said that his country's great running tradition could work against him.

Tergat has already won the world cross country title twice but said: "I know its difficult to predict with so many injuries in running, but I would like to defend my title successfully and go on defending it as long as possible.
"One of the problems in Kenya is that we have so many great runners it is difficult to stay ahead even for two years. It is impossible to double in the Olympic Games, for example."
Apart from winning his second world cross country title this year, Tergat was responsible for dashing Haile Gebrselassie's hopes of an Olympic double.
Tergat ran the second half of the Olympic 10,000 metres final so hard and fast that the Ethiopian, although the winner, was unable to run in the 5,000 metres. Tergat won the 10,000 silver.
He now ends a long year of competition with this new event in Belgrade.
"I like the idea of it combining history and sport," he said.
"It would be good to win the first time but Chellule and Masya will be hard to beat over a short distance.

Tergat's leading rivals in the 6-kms race are compatriots David Challule, the junior world cross country champion, and Benson Masya who recently won the Great North Run half-marathon in England for the fourth time.
A total of 23 runners from 15 countries are competing in the race organised by the Partizan Belgrade multi-sport club and which has a top prize of $5,000.
